problem: Earlier VLN agents are trained on data from a fixed set of scenes, which limits generalization, and their planning and decision making stay implicit. It was also unclear whether an off-the-shelf LLM could understand an interactive embodied world expressed purely in text and carry out a sequential instruction-following navigation task with no training at all.
motivation: LLMs trained on huge language corpora show emergent reasoning and commonsense ability, so they are a plausible route toward a universal embodied agent. Prior LLM-for-navigation work used LLMs only as helpers, for example to parse landmarks (LM-Nav) or to supply object co-occurrence priors (ESC, LGX). The authors want to expose the LLM's explicit reasoning trace during VLN, to see how well it plans and where it breaks.
key_idea: Turn every visual observation into text using visual foundation models, then let a frozen GPT-4 run R2R zero-shot in a ReAct-style loop. At each step it writes an explicit thought and then picks a navigable viewpoint ID, conditioned on a system-principle prompt, the instruction, the current observation text and a summarized history of observations, thoughts and actions.
insight: GPT-4's reasoning traces show real high-level navigation skills: decomposing instructions into sub-goals, grounding landmarks, tracking progress, adjusting plans on unexpected observations, and even drawing a plausible top-down trajectory map from the history. Zero-shot success is still far below trained agents (34 SR vs DUET 72), and the bottleneck is information loss when vision is translated into text and history is summarized, not the reasoning itself. The GPT-3.5 ablations support this: perception quality dominates. Caption granularity matters (FoV45 with 24 views gives SR 16.67 vs 10.19 for FoV60/12 views and 13.89 for FoV30/36 views). Adding Faster R-CNN object detections raises SR from 11.11 to 15.97. Adding object depth ("Obj + Dis") helps a little more (SR 16.67, SPL 11.71 to 13.00), because it fixes the agent stopping as soon as the goal merely comes into view.
method: Visual-to-text translation: at each viewpoint, 24 egocentric views (8 headings at 45° steps × 3 elevations of -30°, 0°, +30°, FoV 45°) are captioned by BLIP-2 ViT-G FlanT5-XL with the prompt 'This is a scene of'. GPT-3.5 then merges the top, middle and down captions of each heading into one sentence.

Object and depth grounding: Faster R-CNN detects objects in each view. The object's relative heading to the agent is computed, and depth is read at the bbox center pixel from the Matterport3D simulator. Only objects within 3 m are kept.
Navigation System Principle prompt: defines the VLN task, the graph-based simulator (move only to existing viewpoint IDs, never fabricate IDs), and the required Thought/Action reasoning format.

ReAct-style reasoning and acting: the action space is extended with free-form language thoughts (Ã = A ∪ R). The LLM outputs a reasoning trace before each action, and these traces are written into the history so plans persist across steps.

Prompt manager: orders the 8 direction descriptions clockwise with the current heading as 'front', attaches navigable viewpoint IDs with relative angles and distances, and assembles the principle, instruction, observation and history into a single prompt. It also parses the LLM Thought/Action output into a simulator move.

History buffer and summarizer: stores (observation, reasoning, action) triples. Past viewpoint observations are compressed to one sentence each by GPT-3.5 to fit the context, while the current viewpoint keeps its full description.

setting.backbone: GPT-4 (frozen) as decision maker; GPT-3.5 used as scene/history summarizer and as the decision LLM in ablations; BLIP-2 ViT-G FlanT5-XL captioner and Faster R-CNN detector (frozen)
setting.observation: panoramic RGB at each viewpoint (24 views: 8 headings × 3 elevations, FoV 45°) converted to text via BLIP-2 captions + Faster R-CNN detections + object depth from simulator; navigable candidate viewpoints with relative heading/distance
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints (LLM outputs a navigable viewpoint ID)
setting.privileged: none beyond the standard R2R discrete setting (nav-graph navigable viewpoints with relative angles/distances); object depth read from simulator depth at bbox center

numbers.extra: BLIP-2 captions + Faster R-CNN objects + depth; GPT-3.5 summarizer

numbers_note: Main result (GPT-4) is on the full R2R val-unseen split (783 trajectories, 11 scenes), and Table 1 prints integers for OSR/SR/SPL. All ablations use GPT-3.5 on a custom 216-instruction set drawn from 61 train and 11 val-unseen scenes, labeled here as a val-unseen subset for the schema. This is the '72-scene / 216-episode' set later reused by MapGPT and others. Instruction generation and top-down map drawing are shown only qualitatively in figures.
results: Zero-shot NavGPT with GPT-4 reaches SR 34 / SPL 29 / NE 6.46 on R2R val-unseen. It far exceeds an untrained DUET (initialized from LXMERT, SR 1) and roughly matches the trained Speaker-Follower (SR 35), but lags well behind pretrained and fine-tuned agents such as HAMT (66) and DUET (72). In the GPT-3.5 ablations, the best perception setup (FoV45 with 24 views, plus objects, plus depth) reaches SR 16.67 / SPL 13.00, against 11.11 / 6.92 for captions alone.
limitations: Large performance gap to supervised VLN agents, caused by information loss when visual scenes become static text and when history is summarized into one sentence per viewpoint; this hurts object tracking and progress judgment (e.g., wrongly believing it has already entered a room).
Relies on costly proprietary GPT-4. The ablations were run only with GPT-3.5 on a small 216-instruction set that mixes training-split scenes.
Works only in the discrete Matterport3D nav-graph setting with pre-computed captions; no continuous environments and no real-robot deployment.
